template_guidance.purpose: Copy this file for a new authored situation. Keep player decisions, delayed actor reactions, response choices, and measurable effects in data.
template_guidance.branch_rule: An action queues its reaction after delay_turns. A reaction without responses is reported automatically. A reaction with responses pauses the scenario until the player chooses one.
template_guidance.effect_fields: confidence_delta, autonomy_delta, legitimacy_delta, treasury_cost, payment_amount_multiplier, payment_due_in, payment_status, export_fraction, levy_per_turn
template_guidance.turns: Turn numbers and effects are gameplay abstractions, not historical dates or quantities.

title: The Caisse, the Nile harvest, and Egyptian debt service

implementation_plan.goal: Show measured changes since the previous turn and the simulation or action that caused them.
implementation_plan.acceptance: Every Guided status has a signed delta and a tooltip with measured contributors.

implementation_plan.goal: Report Britain and France separately and connect Egyptian unrest to live district protest pressure.
implementation_plan.acceptance: Foreign unrest informs the player without interrupting Egypt's turn; Egypt's political pressure changes when protest energy changes.

implementation_plan.goal: Make deferral a dated, more expensive obligation and resolve creditor reactions through the branch tree below.
implementation_plan.acceptance: Deferral produces another payment window; every player action produces a creditor report, and demanding reactions offer visible responses with consequences.

implementation_plan.goal: Show reaction choices, costs, deadlines, and foreign updates in Guided mode and record them in the debrief.
implementation_plan.acceptance: The player can read the next obligation and the reason for each creditor move before choosing a response.

reaction.headline: Creditors note Egypt's emergency maize relief
reaction.body: Britain and France see the reserve release as domestic relief; the scheduled remittance is unchanged.

reaction.headline: Creditors demand an export assurance
reaction.body: The Caisse argues that retaining grain weakens receipts assigned to debt service. Britain and France ask Cairo to restore exports or pledge another source of revenue.

responses.label: Defend food priority
responses.tooltip: Keep grain in local supply. Legitimacy rises 2 points; creditor confidence falls another 5 points.

responses.label: Restore grain exports
responses.tooltip: Remove the special domestic grain retention rule. Creditor confidence rises 10 points, but less grain remains in local supply.

responses.label: Pledge customs revenue
responses.tooltip: Keep domestic grain priority while conceding 10 points of fiscal autonomy. Creditor confidence rises 8 points.

reaction.headline: The Caisse questions lower tax receipts
reaction.body: Creditor delegates request a fiscal account after Cairo lowers cultivator taxes.

responses.label: Submit fiscal account
responses.tooltip: Spend 20 treasury units on the accounting and guarantee process. Creditor confidence rises 5 points; tax relief stays in force.

responses.label: Refuse fiscal review
responses.tooltip: Keep treasury cash and tax relief, but creditor confidence falls 8 points.

reaction.headline: Creditors welcome stronger collection
reaction.body: Britain and France expect more assigned revenue. Creditor confidence rises 5 points, while Egypt's domestic political costs remain.

reaction.headline: The Caisse acknowledges full payment
reaction.body: Britain and France receive the scheduled remittance. No further payment is due during this situation.

reaction.headline: Creditors begin revenue oversight
reaction.body: The Caisse accepts the reduced payment and asks to inspect assigned receipts.

responses.label: Comply with oversight
responses.tooltip: Accept the existing loss of fiscal autonomy. Creditor confidence rises another 5 points.

responses.label: Seek narrower oversight
responses.tooltip: Spend 20 treasury units on negotiations. Recover 10 points of fiscal autonomy, but creditor confidence falls 10 points.

reaction.headline: Creditors demand terms for the revised payment
reaction.body: The missed remittance is now due three turns later at a 10% surcharge. The Caisse asks Cairo for a guarantee.

responses.label: Accept revised terms
responses.tooltip: Keep the new due date and surcharge. Creditor confidence recovers 3 points.

responses.label: Pledge future revenue
responses.tooltip: Reduce the revised payment by 5%, lose 10 points of fiscal autonomy, and restore 10 points of creditor confidence.

responses.label: Reject guarantee
responses.tooltip: Keep the revised due date and cash, but lose another 10 points of creditor confidence. A 5-unit collection levy begins each turn until settlement.

reaction.headline: Creditors assert a claim on customs receipts
reaction.body: Britain and France impose a 10-unit collection levy each turn and reduce Egypt's fiscal autonomy. Cairo can contest the claim or offer an arrears plan.

responses.label: Contest the claim
responses.tooltip: Keep the 10-unit levy and default status. Legitimacy rises 2 points for resisting, while creditor confidence remains at zero.

responses.label: Accept customs control
responses.tooltip: Cut the levy to 5 units per turn and restore 5 points of creditor confidence, but lose another 10 points of fiscal autonomy.

responses.label: Offer arrears plan
responses.tooltip: End the levy and schedule a payment of 125% of the missed remittance three turns from now. Lose 10 points of autonomy and restore 10 points of confidence.
